decisions.question: Adopted: one internal in-process event per write(intent), naming WriteResult.items[] without document contents; above the cap readers reload. The per-database-call event is backend instrumentation. This ships with write(intent) release 2. Multitenant cross-process recovery follows the later B7 durable delivery and bounded full current-state reconciliation contracts; R73 accepts the functional one-host polling reference. decisions.owner: maintainer; framed 2026-10-31, evidence from the profile prototype
decisions.question: Tenancy (one site's data or many) and execution (a resident ddata kept current, or views computed from bounded queries when a write, a timer or a request needs them) are separate axes. Today the subcommand couples them: single is one tenant with a resident ddata; the explicit multitenant API preview now builds request-local loader frames. R73 accepts the functional one-host multitenant evaluator/realtime reference; the independent computed-single prototype has a separate entry bar. A third profile, one tenant computed on demand, would let an independent or low-cost single-tenant site skip the resident ddata without taking on multitenancy or PostgreSQL. It also takes the alarm trigger inside one process, so it does not wait on a cross-process change feed. Default single keeps its resident path. Current multitenant separate processes and the independent computed-single prototype do not select a universal process/host topology. Execution mode is chosen by evidence (maintainer, 2026-10-31): "If the evidence suggested that single tenant needs ddata for cost savings/freemium quotas, then we need to keep that behavior as appropriate." Evidence needed: alarm and properties equality through the profile's own trigger (replay lab, the execution plan §7b cases), and per-tenant memory, CPU per evaluation, database operations per write and per tick, idle cost, and the latest-reading latency, resident against computed, at the full windows the views need (60 h treatments, 24 h device statuses), giving the break-even between the two. Roles are a third axis (maintainer, 2026-10-31, follow-up open): a single-tenant site already runs a headless API v3, so `nightscout single [roles,...]` beside `nightscout multitenant [roles,...]` would give single-tenant and multitenant sites one theory of operations, with the monolithic single-tenant site staying the default.

options.label: Prototype and measure, then choose per profile
options.gains: the execution mode is picked from measured cost and equality; the same views serve single-tenant and multitenant deployment
options.risks: a third start profile to document and test

decisions.short: Identity rules adopted; external feedback remains
decisions.owner: maintainer; current identity specification owns the rules
decisions.question: Proceed under the adopted identity specification and compatibility A/B/C. The server owns _id; clients own identifier, with legacy API v1 forms preserved. Current identifier format is 1–256 characters with URL path encoding; strict/lenient handling is path/configuration-specific. Current resend modes are replace, merge-except-treatments, acknowledge and refuse; bare merge refuses startup. Per-client D20 overrides remain future work. Earlier Loop correspondence is retained as context; waiting for a reply does not block the already merged identifier-first work.
